title: Kenny Clarke's drumming and the shift to ride cymbal timekeeping
summary: Stewart accepted Clarke's off-beat accents, and they agree the move from bass-drum quarter notes to ride cymbal let the bassist be heard, which suited Stewart for bebop.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: How did you like playing with Kenny Clarke at that time? Because he was playing a very unusual drum style, wasn't he?

It was a good sound, yeah, and he -- of course, at times, he played off tempos and what have you quite a bit. But I didn't -- that didn't bother me. I became used to that. Quite a few drummers, they were used to playing off-beat and what have you.
Oh, you mean the accents that they started playing with the --

Even in those days, they started accentuating, you know, their beats and I imagine some of the musicians, the bass players, would kind of have a hard time keeping up with that -- you know, that beat was and still is very important, I think, in music. Whatever type of music it is, especially the good old swing music, but we were accustomed to jazz.

Well, now, when -- a lot of times, when I've heard the older bands, when the drummers were playing quarter notes on the bass drum, I had difficulty a lot of times, at least on the recordings, hearing the bass player.
Because before the bebop style, when (///) the bass and drummers were going (tapping) all the time, I couldn't hear the bass, but --
-- it was, you know. But when the bebop style came in, they started playing on the ride cymbal and using the bass drum for accents.
Right, at least on the bass drum, it
So did the guys at that time -- were they using -- did they use the sock cymbal on two and four then? Do you remember -- they were starting to do that?
So instead of playing (singing) on the sock cymbal with the four quarter notes on the bass drum, they were playing like (singing) on the ride cymbal. (♪ ♪♪ ♪ ♪♪ | ♩ ♩ ♩ ♩)
So could you -- were you able to hear yourself better in that circumstance?
I could hear myself much better.
Uh-huh. So then you were ready for the bebop style.
That's how that man had something to do with -- since you fit it in so well, that may have been the reason why Parker and Gillespie chose to use you and Sid Catlett on the session they did.
